methods.name_en: Two stages of thinking: idea, then processing
methods.use_when: أريد أفكارًا جديدة / الحلول المنطقية نفدت
steps: Name the problem in one sentence before any idea.
Idea stage: generate many alternatives with judgement switched off; write silly ones too.
Do not commit to any irreversible action during the idea stage.
Processing stage: only now evaluate with logic, pick one, plan the steps.
If the pick stalls, go back for one more idea round seeded by the pick.
methods.check: At least 3x more ideas listed than kept, and the evaluation happened after listing ended.
methods.kosif_hook: IdeaForge diverge/converge in A1; think.py ideas

methods.use_when: فكرة إعلان أو قصة أو حل غير تقليدي
steps: Draw 2-4 random nouns from a list you did not choose (seeded, logged).
Never swap a word because it feels unhelpful: choosing by logic kills the randomness.
Exhaust one word (10+ links to the problem) before moving to the next.
Prefer words far from the problem domain; distance yields originality.
Force each association back onto the stated problem and write the idea it suggests.
methods.check: Seed and words are recorded; every idea names the word that triggered it.

methods.name_en: Four ways to mine a word
methods.name_ar: أربع طرق لاستخراج الأفكار من كلمة
methods.use_when: مع REST أو أي كلمة مفتاحية
steps: Association: what the word reminds you of, chained.
Function: what the thing does (protects, hides, rolls, filters) and where else that job is needed.
Direct: read the word as a command (bend, repeat, give) and apply it to the problem.
Pun/humour: sound-alikes and jokes; a relaxed mood loosens patterns.
methods.check: Each word was tried in at least two of the four modes.
methods.kosif_hook: book_methods.py rest prints all four prompts

methods.name_en: Provocation: work forward from a nonsense statement
methods.name_ar: الاستفزاز: ابدأ من جملة غير منطقية
steps: Write a deliberately illogical statement about the subject.
Ask 'could this be true in some sense? why not?' and list readings.
Extract the useful principle from each reading, then drop the nonsense.
methods.check: The final idea stands without the provocation.

steps: List the assumptions everyone accepts about the task.
Ask 'why is it done this way?' until the answer is 'habit' or 'history'.
For each habit-only assumption, design one alternative that removes it.
methods.check: At least one assumption is shown to be habit, not constraint.
methods.kosif_hook: PP-08 impossible puzzles; A12 disconfirming objection

methods.name_en: Be absolutely clear about the problem
steps: Define the problem in one plain sentence.
Break it into its basic components.
Check the obvious solution first; it is often skipped because it looks too simple.
methods.check: The request card has a one-sentence problem and its parts.

methods.use_when: تعديل كود أو كتالوج أو توثيق
steps: Find where the same fact lives twice (code, docs, data, generated files).
Pick one source and generate or reference the rest.
Add a check that fails when copies drift.
methods.check: A builder --check or test catches drift.

steps: Change one component and list what else must change; aim for none.
Keep vendor or model choices behind a thin seam so they can be swapped.
Treat no decision as final: note how you would reverse it.
methods.check: Each risky choice has a written undo path.

steps: Tracer: build a thin end-to-end path that is kept and grown (input to output in real code).
Prototype: build a throwaway to answer one question; say up front it will be discarded.
Never ship a prototype as the product.
methods.check: The plan labels every early build as tracer or prototype.

methods.name_en: Estimate with units, ranges and a model
steps: Choose the unit that matches the precision you mean (days vs weeks).
Build a simple model of the system, list its parameters, compute.
Give a range and record the estimate so you can compare with the actual.
methods.check: Estimate has a range and an assumption list.

steps: Fix the problem, not the blame; do not panic.
Reproduce it with one command before changing code.
Explain the code line by line to someone (rubber duck).
Assume your code is wrong before the compiler, OS or library.
After the fix, add a test so the same bug is found automatically next time.
methods.check: A failing-then-passing test exists for the bug.

methods.name_en: Design by contract, crash early, assert
steps: State preconditions, postconditions and invariants for each routine.
When something impossible happens, stop loudly rather than limp on with bad data.
Use assertions for 'can't happen' cases; exceptions for the truly exceptional.
methods.check: Bad input makes the tool exit non-zero with a clear message.

steps: Know why the code works; write down the assumption it depends on.
Test the assumption instead of trusting it.
Refactor early when the design no longer fits; small steps with tests.
methods.check: Each non-obvious line has a stated, tested reason.

methods.name_en: Dig for requirements; solve the real puzzle
methods.name_ar: احفر عن المتطلبات وحدد القيد الحقيقي
steps: Requirements are dug, not gathered: ask why each one exists.
Separate policy (changes) from requirement (stable); keep policy as data.
For an 'impossible' task, list every constraint and ask which are real; the answer is usually outside the false ones.
Do not start until you are ready, and do not over-specify.
methods.check: Each constraint is tagged real / assumed / policy.
methods.kosif_hook: USIP questions that change the result

methods.name_ar: أتمتة كل شيء واختبار بلا رحمة
steps: Anything done twice gets a script; anything released gets CI.
Test early, often and automatically; a test is not done until it runs in CI.
Find each bug once: every found bug becomes a test.
Test the tests by breaking the code on purpose.
methods.check: CI runs the new test file.

methods.name_en: Broken windows, plain text and pride in the work
methods.name_ar: النوافذ المكسورة والنص الصريح والفخر بالعمل
steps: Fix small rot (bad names, dead code, stale docs) as soon as seen, or board it up with a note.
Keep knowledge in plain text (Markdown, JSON) so tools and people can read it for years.
Care about the craft; sign your work, so quality is personal.
methods.check: No new TODO without an owner; data is human-readable.

steps: Write the hypotheses and the background information I explicitly.
Assign prior plausibilities that use everything known and nothing more.
Update with the product rule: posterior proportional to prior times likelihood.
The same information must give the same answer (consistency).
methods.check: Prior, likelihoods and posterior are written as numbers with their source.

steps: Convert odds to evidence: e = 10 log10(odds) dB.
Each independent datum adds 10 log10(likelihood ratio) dB.
Sum the contributions; 10 dB = 10:1 odds, 20 dB = 100:1.
methods.check: The dB ledger adds up to the stated posterior.
methods.kosif_hook: book_methods.py bayes prints the dB ledger

steps: Never give a hypothesis a prior of exactly 0 or 1.
Add rival explanations such as error, bias or deception; extraordinary data often raise those instead of the headline claim.
Report which hypothesis the data actually moved.
methods.check: At least one rival hypothesis with non-zero prior.

methods.name_en: Maximum entropy and the mind projection fallacy
steps: Pick the least committal distribution that satisfies the known constraints.
Remember probability describes our knowledge, not a property of the object.
When two people disagree on a probability, look for different information, not a different truth.
methods.check: Each assumed distribution names its constraints.

methods.name_en: Five-Factor profile for a character or brand voice
methods.name_ar: ملف العوامل الخمسة لشخصية أو صوت علامة
methods.use_when: بناء شخصية قصة أو نبرة علامة
steps: Rate Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness, Neuroticism (1-5).
Pick two facets per extreme score to make it concrete (e.g. low A: blunt, sceptical).
Translate each score into speech, pace, colour and gesture choices.
Keep the profile fixed across scenes as a HARD LOCK.
methods.check: Every scene's dialogue matches the profile's speech rules.

steps: Consistency lives in stable if-then patterns, not in identical behaviour everywhere (Mischel and Shoda's CAPS).
Write 3-5 rules: 'if criticised in public, then jokes; if criticised alone, then sulks'.
Place scenes that trigger each rule; contrast across situations reveals depth.
methods.check: Each rule is shown at least once on screen.

steps: Decide whether the arc is redemptive (bad turns good) or contaminating (good turns bad).
Give the life story themes of agency (mastery) and communion (connection).
Anchor the turning point in one concrete scene.
methods.check: The emotional arc map names the turn and its theme.

steps: Reward sensitivity drives pursuit; threat sensitivity drives freeze, flight or fight; conflict between goals drives hesitation (Gray's reinforcement sensitivity theory).
Give the character one goal and one fear that collide.
Show hesitation (scanning, delay) where the two meet.
methods.check: The climax puts the goal and fear in the same moment.

methods.use_when: تحفيز جمهور أو مستخدم أو شخصية
steps: Check autonomy (choice), competence (mastery) and relatedness (belonging).
Design the message or scene to satisfy at least one without threatening another.
Avoid controlling language when the goal is lasting motivation.
methods.check: Copy offers a choice and shows a reachable skill.

methods.name_en: Lexical tone words and attachment styles
steps: Traits are encoded in everyday adjectives: pick 3 adjectives per character and ban their opposites in that character's lines.
Give pairs an attachment pattern (secure, anxious, avoidant) to drive closeness and distance in dialogue.
methods.check: A reader can tell who speaks without names.

steps: Trait expression varies across cultures; calibrate to the Arabic audience instead of importing stereotypes.
Use these models for fiction, tone and design only; never diagnose a real person or label anyone with a disorder.
Do not profile real users from their data without consent.
methods.check: No real person is assigned a trait score or diagnosis.

methods.name_en: Versioned setup package before any document
methods.name_ar: حزمة إعداد مُرقّمة قبل أي مستند
steps: Collect chart of accounts (code, nature, currency, active dates), journal register, tax/currency/rounding policy, counterparties, close calendar, report definitions.
Version every rule with effective date and approver.
Refuse to process documents without an open, versioned period.
methods.check: Unique account codes; debits equal credits in sample journals.

methods.name_en: Batch manifest and 'finished' as a control
steps: Hash each file and record upload time, source and period.
Report received, duplicate, unreadable, out-of-period and expected-but-missing.
Keep close locked until the user explicitly confirms completeness and the manifest passes.
methods.check: Manifest shows zero unexplained gaps before close.

steps: Retrieve approved rules and examples for the party.
Let the model interpret meaning (sale, purchase, fee, settlement, transfer) and propose a structured entry.
Validate deterministically: balance, currency, period, tax, account validity.
The model proposes; it never posts. Posting needs approval, privilege and an idempotency key.
methods.check: Every proposal carries source region, rule version and validation result.

methods.name_en: New counterparty: ask, learn scoped, constrain
methods.name_ar: طرف جديد: اسأل وتعلم بنطاق وقيّد
steps: Similar names do not prove identity; create a temporary party record.
Ask one specific question: new or existing? nature? VAT recoverable? should it recur?
Store the answer as a scoped, versioned rule with approver; watch early repetitions.
methods.check: No silent generalisation from a single answer.

steps: Build an event key from invoice number, party, date, amount and currency, plus file hashes.
A bank receipt that matches an invoice is a settlement (debit bank, credit receivable), never new revenue.
Support one-to-many and partial matches; show the difference instead of forcing a match.
Own-bank transfers and bank fees have their own treatments.
methods.check: Zero duplicate revenue in the test set.

methods.name_en: Integer minor units and deterministic checks
steps: Store money as integers of the smallest unit (halala for SAR), never binary floats.
Declare rounding; tax = base x rate under that rule.
Reject unbalanced entries; check open period and unused idempotency key.
Derive balances from lines; never type totals into reports.
methods.check: Replay gives byte-identical numbers.

methods.name_ar: خريطة المعايير: من المتطلب إلى الضابط
steps: Record framework, edition, effective date and paragraph link for every treatment.

IFRS 15 revenue (contract, obligations, price, allocation, timing); IFRS 9 classification and expected credit loss; IAS 2 inventory at lower of cost and NRV; IAS 16 PPE and depreciation; IAS 8 policy vs estimate vs error; IAS 12 current and deferred tax; IFRS 16 leases; IAS 36 impairment; IAS 7 cash-flow classes; IFRS 18 presentation (annual periods from 1 Jan 2027).
Audit side: ISA 315 risk, ISA 500 evidence, ISA 530 sampling; COSO for controls.
Turn every standard-level claim into a data requirement, a deterministic check or a human decision.
methods.check: No treatment without its standard link; the accountant signs judgement.
methods.kosif_hook: A6; live check of ifrs.org before relying on an effective date

methods.name_en: Evaluation, release gates and Saudi controls
steps: Test on de-identified recurring, new, ambiguous, poor-scan and adversarial cases; an independent accountant signs gold entries first.
Gates: accuracy on recurring cases, 100% amount accuracy, zero duplicates, 100% evidence coverage; any unbalanced posting, lost original, cross-tenant leak or unapproved posting stops release.
Treat document text as untrusted (prompt injection); least privilege; PDPL minimisation and transfer review; ZATCA e-invoice fields.
Keep ERP write access closed during the pilot.
methods.check: Release report lists every gate with its measured value.

methods.name_en: v8 runtime router mapped to USIP levels
methods.use_when: طلب صورة أو فيديو أو برومنت
steps: SINGLE_IMAGE (explicit 'one image only') = L0/L1: answer at once.
SCOPED_ASSET (a code like SHOT-05-END) = narrow follow-up: edit that asset only.
CONTINUE ('next') = resume the chosen plan's next node.
AUDIT (failed image or prompt) = diagnosis with the v8 rubric.
FULL_WORKFLOW (a story idea, even one sentence) = L2: brief, plans A/B/C and A17 questions inside one report.
methods.check: The level is stated in the report.

steps: Clarity: one meaning per noun, adjective and verb; two readers would get the same picture.
Replace hollow words (beautiful, nice, cool, amazing, great, good) with exact description.
Context: time (hour, season, era), place (setting, energy), emotion, motion, narrative purpose.
Specificity: HARD LOCK identity and story element; MEDIUM light and base colours; SOFT LATITUDE expression and fine details.
methods.check: book_methods.py clarity scores >= 8 / 8 / 7 before generating.

steps: Project card: idea, emotional arc, duration, platform, tool, style, aspect ratio, language, assumptions.
Block 1 assets (CHAR/ENV codes with emotional constant and context); block 2 shots with 6Q (who, what, where, when, why, how); block 3 videos with mood arc, motion style, sound notes.
Negative prompting: say what must not appear.
methods.check: Each shot answers all six questions in one sentence each.

methods.name_en: Timed emotional arc and platform tone
steps: Map start, middle, end and payoff emotions onto seconds (e.g. 0-5 s build, 5-20 s intensify, 20-25 s turn, 25-30 s payoff).
Pick register by platform: casual and direct for TikTok, literary for cinema, persuasive and fast for ads.
Register: formal/documentary, poetic, technical, casual.
methods.check: Cut points in the edit match the arc timings.

methods.use_when: فيلم قصيدة أو دعاء أو بيت شعر
steps: One verse (bayt) per visual beat; first hemistich (sadr) and second (ajuz) as two lines or two halves.
Never split a hemistich across cards; the rhyme letter (rawiy) ends every ajuz, so align ends.
Hold time follows recitation, not word count; sync to words.json when audio exists.
Check diacritics on the source before animating; a wrong vowel changes meaning or metre.
methods.check: Every card holds whole hemistichs and the rhyme letter is consistent.

methods.name_en: Occasion poem and verse fable as formats
methods.use_when: فيلم مناسبة أو قصة أخلاقية للأطفال
steps: Occasion poem: event, reflection, maxim (hikma), address to the audience; Shawqi's diwan is organised largely by events and occasions.
Verse fable on an animal's tongue: short scene, dialogue, closing moral; suits kids' explainer videos.
Quote Shawqi's public-domain verses with attribution and check them against a rendered page.
methods.check: The moral or maxim lands in the final beat.

methods.name_ar: خطر استخراج النص العربي من PDF
steps: Text layers in Arabic PDFs often swap glyphs: this diwan extracts 'أمري' for 'أمير' and 'املؤمنني' for 'المؤمنين'; the v8 spec PDF extracted as unreadable presentation forms.
Normalise with NFKC, then compare a sample against the rendered page image.
Never quote Arabic from a PDF text layer without that visual check.
methods.check: A rendered-page check is recorded for any quoted Arabic.

methods.use_when: درس أو دورة أو فيديو تعليمي
steps: Open each unit with 3-5 'you will be able to…' outcomes in plain verbs.
Hook with one strong photo and a personal question before any rule.
End with a check that maps one task to each outcome.
methods.check: Every outcome has a matching practice task.

steps: Learners find the pattern in a real text before being told it (guided discovery).
They check against a short reference page.
Controlled practice, then the learner applies it to their own life.
Pair talk and partner swaps recycle the language and find common ground.
methods.check: The lesson has a discovery step before the rule.

steps: Separate scene heading, stage direction and dialogue on distinct lines.
Directions in present tense and brief; dialogue carries character.
No content from the excluded source is used; this is standard script practice.
methods.check: Each line is one of the three types.

methods.use_when: «مش لاقي اسم/فكرة تجمع الحاجات دي» / تصنيف جديد
steps: Gather 5-10 typical examples of the thing.
List what each has; keep only the features every example shares.
Name the pattern in one line: that is the new concept.
Test it on a borderline case and on a non-example; tighten it until both are judged right.
methods.check: The concept has a one-line definition and passes at least one borderline and one non-example test.

methods.name_en: Analyse a concept in three steps
methods.use_when: كلمة في الطلب غامضة أو محمّلة (جودة، فخم، احترافي)
steps: Collect examples where the word clearly applies.
Pull out the shared features; they are what the user really means.
Test each feature with a case that has it and a case that lacks it.
methods.check: The vague word is replaced on the request card by 2-4 checkable features.

methods.use_when: دمج أفكار أو مهارات أو مراجع في شيء جديد
steps: Pick the kind: a new concept, a reformulated pattern, gathering ideas under an existing concept, or fusing two concepts.
For a fusion, shift the emphasis to a different part of each pattern before joining them.
Compare the two from a perspective neither normally takes.
Keep the fusion only if it explains or does something neither part did alone.
methods.check: The plan names its synthesis kind and the gain over each part.

steps: Keep a list of about 10 trigger questions for the field (what do we mean by X, why did it happen, what if...).
Answer each from the view of every party involved.
Then answer at each level: person, group, system.
Only then structure the ideas: map conceptual and causal links and look for convergences that suggest a testable hypothesis.
methods.check: Ideas came from at least 3 perspectives and 2 levels before any was judged.

methods.name_en: Four ways to adapt a stuck structure
steps: Change the structure: rearrange or drop one link.
Approach it from a different direction (from the result back, or from another party).
Start from a different point in the chain.
Create a new structure, often from an analogy whose causal shape matches (argue from an analogy only where a causal link holds).
methods.check: At least two of the four were tried and written down before giving up.
methods.kosif_hook: think.py ladder; plan C must differ in engine

steps: Options as rows, factors as columns.
Score each option on each factor (0-5).
Weight factors 1-5; if unsure, compare factors two at a time and count wins.
Multiply, add, rank; then check the winner with a mental simulation of how others will respond.
Convert any risk numbers to frequencies (out of 100 or 1000) and keep the base rate in view.
methods.check: The pick comes from a written grid; weights came from a stated method; base rates are shown.

methods.name_en: The look serves the story, inside budget
methods.name_ar: الشكل البصري في خدمة القصة وداخل الميزانية
methods.use_when: بداية أي فيلم أو إعلان أو برومبت فيديو
steps: Write the look in one paragraph from the director's intent: format, lensing, light, colour, movement.
List the creative and cost trade-offs of each option plainly.
Lock the look before shooting or generating; every shot is checked against it.
methods.check: A written look sheet exists before the first shot or generation.
methods.kosif_hook: A8 Motion Brain; A17 story charter; kling director

methods.name_en: Shutter, motion blur and frame rate
methods.use_when: حركة تبدو متقطعة أو مصطنعة، أو مطابقة لقطات
steps: Default to a 180-degree shutter: exposure time = 1 / (2 x fps), e.g. 1/48 s at 24 fps, 1/60 s at 30 fps.
Keep pans slow enough for the frame rate (the manual tabulates safe panning speeds); fast pans at 24-30 fps strobe.
When matching a screen or light flicker, pick a frame rate and shutter whose exposure divides the source refresh evenly.
State fps and shutter in generation prompts and render settings.
methods.check: fps and shutter are stated and consistent across shots; no strobing pans.

methods.name_en: Focus and depth of field by numbers
methods.use_when: تحديد ما يكون حادًا في الكادر
steps: Hyperfocal distance H = f^2 / (N x c), all in the same units (f focal length, N f-stop, c circle of confusion).
Focusing at H keeps everything from H/2 to infinity acceptably sharp.
For a shallow look use longer focal length, wider stop or closer focus; say which in the prompt.
methods.check: Any depth-of-field claim in a plan or prompt names focal length, stop and focus distance.
methods.kosif_hook: A8; 3D camera rigs; prompt specificity KV-02

methods.use_when: مشهد ليلي بدون إضاءة ليلية حقيقية
steps: Shoot or generate under strong sun and blue sky.
Use low-angle back-cross light; avoid flat front light, and pure backlight only for wide shots.
Underexpose and keep the sky out or darkened; grade cool afterwards.
Keep enough density to grade down; a thin original can't be made rich later.
methods.check: The night look survives a grade without crushed faces or a bright sky.
methods.kosif_hook: colour matching in export standard; Higgsfield/Kling prompts

methods.name_en: Colour pipeline from set to grade
methods.use_when: مطابقة ألوان بين لقطات أو مصادر
steps: Carry one colour decision per shot (slope, offset, power, saturation, like an ASC CDL) instead of baking looks into files.
Work in one managed colour space end to end (ACES-style) and convert once at delivery.
Measure, don't eyeball: compare against a reference frame or chart.
methods.check: Every graded shot has a recorded, reversible colour decision.

steps: Confirm the problem definition, the requirements and the architecture are stable enough to build on.
The later a defect is found, the more it costs; fix upstream first.
Write down what is unknown and how it will be resolved.
methods.check: A short pre-build note lists problem, requirements, design and open unknowns.

steps: Write the routine's purpose and steps as plain-language comments first.
Review the comments as the design; only then fill in code under each.
Keep the comments as documentation; delete steps that turned out wrong.
methods.check: Each non-trivial routine started from reviewed pseudocode.

methods.use_when: مدخلات من مستخدم أو ملف أو شبكة
steps: Validate everything that crosses a trust boundary; trust inside the barricade.
Use assertions for things that must never happen and error handling for things that can.
Fail loudly in development, gracefully in production.
methods.check: Inputs from outside are checked at one place; asserts never replace input validation.
methods.kosif_hook: PP-06 contracts and crash-early; A6 security

steps: Combine techniques: reviews or inspections catch defects tests miss, and the reverse.
Before optimising, measure where the time really goes; change one thing, measure again.
Keep the readable version unless the measured gain is worth it.
methods.check: Every optimisation has before/after numbers; every change had at least one review pass.

methods.use_when: تصنيف أو تعريف أو فهرسة مفاهيم
steps: For any term, ask which of five it is relative to a thing: genus (الجنس), species (النوع), differentia (الفصل), property (الخاصة) or common accident (العرض العام).
Essential answers (genus, species, differentia) say what a thing is; property and accident only describe it.
Use the split to build catalogues: families as genus, items as species, the distinguishing feature as differentia.
methods.check: Each catalogue level is labelled as genus, species or differentia, and descriptive tags are kept apart.

methods.use_when: تعريف مصطلح أو قدرة أو مهارة بدقة
steps: Name the nearest genus (the closest wider kind).
Add the differentia that separates it from its siblings.
Check: the definition fits every case of the thing and nothing else; a definition by property alone is only a description (رسم), not a full definition (حد).
methods.check: The definition is 'nearest kind + distinguishing feature' and passes the fits-all/fits-only test.
